tasks.short: Compare marketing channels and tactics, explain their results, and recommend the next tests.

steps.what: Collect campaign results and downstream outcomes from the {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, and {CRM}.
Match campaign identifiers, dates, costs, and conversions in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Check missing conversions, inconsistent definitions, and unusual changes against source records.
Interpret channel performance against objectives, audience differences, attribution limits, and previous tests.
Assemble charts, comparisons, and recommendations into a performance report in the {DOCS}.
Agree which tactics to test, retain, or stop with the marketing manager.

tasks.design: Configure connectors from the {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, and {CRM}; deterministic jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} join results to the campaign budget ledger and run quality checks. A {BI} dashboard exposes definitions, exceptions, and source records, while a template generator prepares the performance report in the {DOCS}. People interpret the evidence and approve test plans in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel definitions and campaign identifiers differ. Manual reconciliation bridges the systems, while causal interpretation still needs judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors cover much of the collection. AI-assisted coding can shorten development of joins, validation rules, and report templates without changing attribution limits.
tasks.still_hard: Offline outcomes, delayed conversions, consent-related gaps, and channel overlap can prevent a reliable causal comparison.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a convincing channel story from a defensible conclusion, then choosing a useful test.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting and formatting results to investigating anomalies and designing tests. The manager can gain delegated authority to select tests within an agreed budget; larger reallocations still need approval.

reach.task: Design a channel experiment with a clear comparison group.
reach.learn: Experiment design, conversion lag, attribution bias, and stopping rules.

reach.task: Test whether channel differences reflect different audience needs.

evidence.claim: Funnel provides channel connectors, standardised marketing data, and automated reports.
Collection and reporting can be automated while causal interpretation and test selection remain human.
Direct-marketing objections also cover related profiling and must be respected.

assumptions: The steps describe a typical mid-size European company, not a verified customer workflow.
The time shares use the supplied priors but assign substantial time to reconciliation and interpretation.
Remaining-time percentages and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Existing connectors can retrieve the main sources; unsupported sources would increase integration work.
The access range includes GDPR review and any employee consultation required by national rules; individual staff scoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Which channel connectors and reporting capabilities are already licensed?
How consistently are campaign identifiers recorded across systems?
Which downstream outcomes are measurable and available to marketing?
Who may approve tests and budget reallocations?
Does the proposed reporting expose identifiable employee activity?
research_questions: Which attribution method is defensible for the available channels and conversion delays?
Can aggregate reporting answer the main questions with less personal data?
new_work: Investigate failed joins, missing outcomes, and unexpected metric changes.
Maintain campaign mappings, metric definitions, and report templates.
Review connector changes and access permissions.
Record test hypotheses and compare subsequent results with the original decision.

tasks.short: Align marketing contributors, organise campaign delivery, resolve creative disagreements, and approve launch readiness.

steps.what: Consolidate objectives, requests, and constraints from the {EMAIL} into a campaign brief.

loop.input: Selected campaign requests, business objectives, brand guidelines, and available budget.
loop.output: A structured campaign brief with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields; trace constraints to sources; flag conflicting or unsupported statements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per brief; unresolved conflicts go to the advertising manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests contain free text and conflicting instructions that fixed field mappings cannot resolve.

steps.what: Agree campaign direction, responsibilities, and trade-offs with contributors.
Create delivery tasks, dependencies, owners, and review dates in the {PROJECT}.
Chase progress by the {EMAIL} and copy replies into the {PROJECT}.
Review campaign assets with designers and resolve creative disagreements.
Check readiness and authorise campaign launch in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A bounded extractor prepares a campaign brief in the {DOCS} from selected requests in the {EMAIL} and {CHAT}. Configure delivery templates, contributor updates, dependency alerts, and readiness checks in the {PROJECT}, removing duplicate status copying. People agree direction, resolve creative disagreements, and approve the launch before publishing or sending through the {CMS}, {ADS}, or {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive in different formats, and teams keep separate status records. Software can organise delivery but cannot settle creative or capacity disputes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project workflows handle templates and approvals. Bounded extraction and AI-assisted coding make brief preparation and missing integrations cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Contributors must keep their delivery records current. Creative disagreements, changing priorities, and external dependencies still require conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Building commitment across specialists and resolving trade-offs without losing the campaign's purpose.

ambition.what: Weekly creative blocker clinic for small campaign teams

tasks.altitude: The week contains less status chasing and more brief clarification and creative problem-solving. The manager can gain delegated authority to resolve delivery trade-offs within the approved campaign scope.

reach.task: Review a creative brief before concept development starts.
reach.learn: Visual constraints, revision costs, asset specifications, and useful feedback.

reach.task: Plan the review sequence for campaign copy.
reach.learn: Editorial stages, claim substantiation, version control, and publication readiness.

evidence.claim: HubSpot offers campaign planning and branded-content capabilities.
Project templates, contributor updates, and approval workflows can reduce coordination paperwork.
EU AI Act Article 50 contains transparency duties for specified AI interactions and synthetic content.

assumptions: Contributors can update a shared delivery record instead of maintaining parallel status threads.
The meeting-heavy prior is retained; preparation and paperwork change more than the conversations.
The eliminated step covers routine duplicate chasing; resolving a real blocker remains human work.
Remaining-time percentages and build ranges are estimates.
The access range includes GDPR review and consultation required by national rules if the workflow changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which delivery templates and approval features already exist in the {PROJECT}?
Can external contributors access the relevant project records?
Who approves creative assets, claims, expenditure, and launch?
Are status records used to evaluate individual employees?
Which synthetic assets or interactive AI features are included in campaigns?
research_questions: Which brief fields prevent the most avoidable revisions?
Which readiness checks can be automated without encouraging superficial approvals?
Which AI transparency duties apply to the planned campaign formats?
new_work: Review extracted briefs and resolve contradictory requests.
Maintain delivery templates, dependencies, and readiness checks.
Handle stale contributor updates and genuine delivery blockers.
Check that final assets satisfy applicable disclosure and consent requirements.

tasks.short: Research consumer opinions and buying habits, then choose audiences supported by the evidence.

steps.what: Define research questions, participant criteria, and collection methods in the {DOCS}.
Retrieve buying patterns and public consumer commentary from the {CRM}, {ECOMMERCE}, and {SOCIAL}.
Invite eligible consumers and arrange research sessions through the {EMAIL}.
Interview consumers about needs, purchase decisions, and reactions to proposed offers.
Clean buying data and link permitted research responses in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Code opinions, compare buying patterns, and document themes with supporting evidence.

loop.input: Permitted research responses, coding framework, and deterministic buying-pattern summaries.
loop.output: Coded responses and draft themes linked to supporting and contradictory evidence.
loop.check: Validate source references; calculate counts deterministically; review a sample, contradictions, and uncoded responses.
loop.stop: One coding pass and one correction pass per batch; ambiguous responses stay uncoded for analyst review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Consumer language varies, and themes often depend on context beyond keyword rules.

steps.what: Choose target audiences with the marketing manager, accounting for uncertainty and practical reach.
Prepare the research report and audience definitions in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure permitted exports from the {CRM}, {ECOMMERCE}, and {SOCIAL}, then clean and aggregate them on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded classifier proposes evidence-linked themes, and a template generator assembles the research report in the {DOCS}; the {WORKFLOW} prepares invitations for approval. People design the research, conduct interviews, and choose audience recommendations, with activation approval handled in the campaign workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Buying data and consumer language live in different places. Manual coding is slow, and weak samples cannot be repaired by faster processing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and listening tools support collection. Bounded classification can accelerate qualitative coding while retaining source evidence and analyst review.
tasks.still_hard: Representative recruitment, contextual interpretation, data rights, and distinguishing stated preferences from actual behaviour remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Asking a useful follow-up question and recognising when a proposed audience rests on biased or thin evidence.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward interviewing, checking surprising themes, and designing follow-up research. The manager can gain authority to commission small validation studies within an agreed research budget.

reach.task: Build and audit a participant sample.
reach.learn: Sampling bias, questionnaire design, qualitative coding, and uncertainty.

reach.task: Validate a buying-habit hypothesis against purchase cohorts.
reach.learn: Repeat purchases, returns, seasonality, and cohort definitions.

evidence.claim: Coosto supports social listening, emotion analysis, and monitoring dashboards.
Neleman's vendor case reports improved email outcomes after segmentation; it does not establish research validity.
Bounded coding can assist qualitative analysis, but sample quality and interpretation still need people.
An objection to direct marketing requires stopping the related direct-marketing processing, including profiling.

assumptions: The company uses both existing behavioural evidence and occasional consumer interviews.
The unstructured-input prior supports a bounded coding loop; participant conversations remain human.
Research participation does not automatically authorise subsequent marketing.
Deterministic cleaning links responses only where the documented purpose and lawful basis permit it.
Remaining-time percentages and build ranges are estimates.
The access range covers GDPR purpose, retention, and participant-information review, plus consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which consumer datasets are available and licensed for this purpose?
What lawful bases, participant notices, and retention periods apply?
How are participants recruited, and which groups are missing?
Are sensitive characteristics present in responses or proposed audience definitions?
Who approves audience activation and research invitations?
research_questions: How accurately does the coding loop preserve minority views and contradictory responses?
Which behavioural measures best test the stated consumer preferences?
When are aggregate audience definitions sufficient without individual profiling?
new_work: Review coded responses, ambiguous themes, and contradictory evidence.
Maintain the coding framework and evaluate changes to the model.
Audit sample coverage and commission missing research.
Maintain permitted-use rules, retention schedules, and participant records.
Carry uncertainty and evidence limitations into campaign briefs.

tasks.short: Track campaign spending and responses, reconcile discrepancies, and assess progress against objectives and suitable benchmarks.

steps.what: Retrieve approved budgets, commitments, and booked expenses from the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}.
Retrieve spend and campaign responses from the {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, and {CRM}.
Update the campaign budget ledger and calculate response rates in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Resolve missing invoices, timing differences, and unmatched campaign costs with the finance team.
Assess budget variances and response rates against campaign objectives and comparable industry benchmarks.
Discuss exceptions and approve corrective spending decisions with the marketing manager.

tasks.design: Configure shared feeds from the {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT}, {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, and {CRM} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic calculations maintain the campaign budget ledger, reconcile overlapping spend sources, and show response rates and exceptions in the {BI}; the {WORKFLOW} routes proposed corrections to finance. People assess benchmark relevance and approve spending decisions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance booking dates differ from channel reporting dates, and commitments are easily missed. Campaign cost allocations often depend on manually maintained mappings.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors, scheduled calculations, and existing approval features already cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can speed up the remaining reconciliation and exception routing.
tasks.still_hard: Shared agency costs, late invoices, tax treatment, currency differences, and inconsistent benchmark definitions still need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether a variance needs action, reflects timing, or reveals a flawed campaign assumption.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from updating trackers to resolving cost exceptions and challenging campaign economics. The manager can gain authority to initiate corrective actions within delegated limits; spending changes retain their approval requirements.

reach.task: Prepare a campaign portfolio spending forecast.
reach.learn: Commitments, accruals, conversion lag, and scenario assumptions.

reach.task: Translate campaign economics into a channel pacing recommendation.
reach.learn: Daily pacing, marginal returns, and conversion-quality checks.

evidence.claim: Funnel supports standardised channel data and automated marketing reporting.
Spotler provides campaign data and response-tracking capabilities.
Ledger reconciliation and response-rate calculations can be deterministic; this task needs no model loop.
ePrivacy rules govern marketing email and consent for non-essential cookies, affecting response measurement.

assumptions: The company uses finance records for booked expenditure and channel reports for operational pacing.
The structured-input prior supports deterministic calculations; benchmark selection and corrective decisions remain human.
Channel spend and booked invoices are reconciled rather than added together.
The budget ledger is an analytical record; this solution does not post accounting entries or execute payments.
Remaining-time percentages and build ranges are estimates.
The access range includes finance permissions, GDPR review, and employee consultation required by national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Are campaign codes available on invoices, commitments, and channel records?
Which costs include tax, fees, currency conversion, or shared agency charges?
How quickly do commitments and invoices reach the {ERP}?
Which benchmarks are licensed and genuinely comparable?
What spending limits and correction approvals apply?
research_questions: Which reporting windows avoid misleading comparisons between spend and delayed responses?
Which reconciliation rules prevent double counting across channel and finance feeds?
Which exception thresholds identify actionable overspend without excessive alerts?
new_work: Review unmatched costs, late invoices, and reconciliation exceptions.
Maintain allocation rules, currency handling, and metric definitions.
Refresh benchmark sources and document comparability limits.
Maintain alert thresholds and approval routing.
Verify that approved budget actions are reflected in subsequent campaign results.

role.altitude: The role spends less time assembling evidence and chasing routine updates, and more time choosing tests, improving briefs, and resolving creative and financial trade-offs. Decision rights can expand to small experiments and corrective actions within explicit delegated limits.
reach: Search Marketing Strategist: design experiments and turn evidence into channel pacing decisions.
Market Research Analyst: strengthen sampling and qualitative evidence checks.
Graphic Designer: improve briefs and the quality of creative feedback.
Marketing Manager: prepare campaign portfolio forecasts and spending recommendations.
role.ambitious_version: Run a repeatable campaign learning service: connect audience evidence, creative hypotheses, delivery readiness, and campaign economics so teams can select better experiments and make timely spending decisions.
